_readme: The organisation's own context: what is signed, who is allowed to do what,
which ranges are lab, which destinations are sanctioned.
This is TRUSTED input. Unlike everything in an alert, it is not written by
whoever triggered the alert — it comes from asset inventory, the identity
provider and change management. That is precisely why it can be used to
decide that something was authorised, and why an attacker cannot add
themselves to it by naming a process cleverly.
In a real deployment this file is generated from the CMDB, the IdP's service
account list, and the change calendar. Here it is hand-written to match the
synthetic corpus, and every claim in it is fictional.
AUTHORISATION IS SCOPED. `max_privilege` is the point of the design: knowing
an account is not the same as that account being allowed to do the specific
thing observed. svc_helpdesk is a known automation account and is still not
permitted to touch Domain Admins — an unscoped allowlist would have excused
exactly that, which is the confused-deputy failure this file is shaped to
avoid. The first scorecard run with an unscoped list produced a missed true
positive on TP-05.
Without this file Bishop still runs — it simply cannot distinguish
'authorised' from 'malicious', so an approved red-team exercise reads as a
genuine intrusion. That is the correct failure direction.

svc_intune.note: Endpoint management. Provisions workstations and sets local group membership during onboarding.

svc_veeam.note: Backup service. Archives file shares to the backup volume nightly.

svc_build.note: Build agent. Fetches toolchains from the internal artefact server.

svc_helpdesk.note: Helpdesk automation. Resets passwords and unlocks accounts. NOT permitted to change domain group membership.

system.note: Local system, used by management agents.

scanner_sources.10.20.5.99: Authenticated vulnerability scanner. Weekly credentialed sweep; failed logins against test accounts are expected and the rule should exclude this source.

_never_block_readme: Destinations that may never be blocked estate-wide, whatever an alert says.
The executor already refuses to block a destination this incident never
contacted. That bounds the shape of the target and not the harm, because the
dangerous case is well-formed: an adversary on a host they already own emits
thirty high-entropy DNS queries under the identity provider's domain. The
tunnelling detector fires, correctly reports the registrable parent, and the
plan proposes blocking it. An analyst reading thirty encoded queries under
that name approves, and the estate loses single sign-on.
Nothing has malfunctioned there — the guard has been used as designed. The
only bound that holds is one the adversary cannot write into an alert, which
is why it lives in this file with everything else that comes from the CMDB
rather than from a payload. Blocking one of these is a decision a human takes
outside Bishop.
A registrable domain here also covers its subdomains, and its superdomains:
blocking a parent cuts every child, so listing `update.microsoft.com` also
refuses `microsoft.com`.
NAMES DO NOT COVER THEIR ADDRESSES. Bishop does not resolve - a lookup is a
network call on a control path, and the answer is steerable by an adversary
who controls DNS for a name they own. An entry that is an address or a CIDR
range is matched against `block_ip`; a name is not. List the ranges that
matter.
_public_suffixes_readme: Registry boundaries this organisation adds to the committed Public Suffix
The world's boundaries come from the PSL and no deployment should be editing
them. This list is for the ones only this organisation has: an internal TLD,
a lab namespace, anything delegated inside the estate. Blocking one of those
is the same outage as blocking `com`.
Adding a suffix here refuses that name and PERMITS names under it: with
`mycorp` listed, `mycorp` stops being blockable and `db.mycorp` starts. That
is the intent - it is how an internal TLD gets treated as a registry - but it
is not the one-directional guarantee an earlier draft of this note claimed,
and a claim about a control property the code does not have is exactly what
went wrong three times in src/bishop/graph/containment.py. Add only
